_note: French pronunciation drills by first language, for /culture/erreurs and the Aussprache-Check. Each drill practises one French sound or pattern that is hard from a particular first language (transfer, see fehler-nach-sprache.json). `pairs`: minimal pairs, the first word is the target, the second is what often comes out instead or a word to tell it apart from; both are real French words. `words`: practice words without a partner. `sentence`: to repeat, scored like the Aussprache-Check; it contains one word of every pair. `fehler`: the ids of the mistakes in fehler-nach-sprache.json that this drill practises (the other side of their `drill`; checked by pnpm check:aussprache). Standard French of France; the file's `variety` covers every drill, and `frCA` says where Québec differs. Languages: English, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian and Arabic (content-plan §5.6); Russian, Ukrainian and Chinese drills were removed with the Spanish course. Drill ids are new (r, u-ou, nasal, eu, e-muet, liaison, enchainement, silent, s-z, ch-j, b-v, aspiration, stress, double, voiced-final, p-b, vowels, h). The pairs hold only distinctions the standard makes: no brin/brun, and é/è are not paired. Audio: public/audio/muttersprache/<slug>.mp3 once fr-FR recordings exist; until then the browser voice reads them.

r.title: The French r
r.tip: The French r is made at the back of your mouth. Keep the tip of your tongue down behind your bottom teeth, lift the back of your tongue towards the soft palate and let the air rub through, like a soft gargle. A gentle cough or the “g” of “go” is a good start. Not the English r, not a tongue-tip trill.
r.sentence: Elle rit au lit, car elle aime lire ce long roman.

frCA.note: In Québec, tu and ti are often affricated (“tsu”, “tsi”). Normal there; in France and in exams, say tu with a clean t.

u-ou.title: u or ou?
u-ou.tip: ou is as in “you”: lips round, tongue back. u is different: say “ee” (i), then round your lips without moving your tongue. Feel your tongue stay forward and your lips make a small circle. Swap them and you say a different word: tu / tout, rue / roue.
u-ou.sentence: Tu as vu la rue, il y a du monde dessus.

frCA.note: In Québec the nasal vowels are often longer and more open than in France, and in long syllables they glide a little (vin, vent).

nasal.title: Nasal vowels: an, on, in
nasal.tip: A nasal vowel is a vowel said with the air going through your nose and the n left out. an/en: mouth open, tongue low (vent). on: lips round (bon). in/ain: lips spread, tongue forward (vin). Hold the vowel and don't close it with an n or a “g”. Say bonne, and the n comes back, since it is followed by a vowel.
nasal.sentence: Il y a du vent, mais le pain est bon sur ce banc.

eu.title: eu: a third rounded vowel
eu.tip: Say é (as in été), keep your tongue where it is and round your lips. That is eu (deux, peu). Before r and other consonants it is more open (peur, sœur). It is not ou: deux is not doux.
eu.sentence: Pour deux euros, j'ai un peu peur.

e-muet.title: e muet: weak or silent e
e-muet.tip: At the end of a word e is silent: table is “tabl”. In short words (le, de, ce, je, que) and in the first syllable (demain, petit) it is weak: drop it if the syllable before it ends in a vowel, keep it (short, like eu) when you would otherwise get three consonants in a row. Don't mix it up with é or with les, des, ces, which have a clear é.
e-muet.sentence: Je regarde le chat de Léa et les chats de ces voisins.

liaison.title: Liaison
liaison.tip: A silent final consonant is said before a vowel sound, and it joins the next word. s and x sound as z (les amis, deux ans), d as t (grand arbre), f as v (neuf heures). It is required after a determiner, a pronoun before the verb and short words like en, dans, très. It is forbidden after et and before a h aspiré (les héros). Be careful with a pause: the link is in the voice, not in a gap.
liaison.sentence: Ils ont des amis en France, et ils les voient en été.

enchainement.title: Enchaînement: no breaks between words
enchainement.tip: French flows. A spoken consonant at the end of a word slides over onto the next vowel: il a = “i-la”, elle est = “è-lè”, une amie = “u-na-mi”. Don't stop your voice before a vowel (that small stop is a glottal stop). Say a whole group as one long word.
enchainement.sentence: Elle a une amie qui habite avec elle à Annecy.

silent.title: Silent letters at the end
silent.tip: Many final letters are silent: t, d, s, x, p, z, and -er, -ez, -ent of verbs. petit is “peti”, grand is “gran”, ils parlent is “il parle”. The feminine brings the consonant back: petit / petite, grand / grande, chaud / chaude. c, r, f, l are often said (sac, mer, neuf, bol).
silent.sentence: Le petit garçon boit un thé chaud dans une grande tasse.

s-z.title: s or z: poisson or poison?
s-z.tip: Between two vowels one s is z: poison, cuisine, maison. A double ss is s: poisson, dessert. At the start of a word, s is s, and z is z: zéro, zone. A ç also gives s: français. Keep your voice on for z, and off for s: put your hand on your throat.
s-z.sentence: Le poisson, le dessert et un coussin: voilà mon dimanche.

ch-j.title: ch and j
ch-j.tip: ch is the sh of “shop”: chat, chou. j, and g before e or i, is the voiced version: the s of “measure”. Keep your voice on: jour, rouge, manger. It is never “dj” as in “jam”, and never a rasp at the back of your mouth.
ch-j.sentence: Ce chou est cher, mais Léa joue au marché.

b-v.title: b or v?
b-v.tip: For b, your two lips close. For v, your top teeth touch your bottom lip lightly, and your voice buzzes. French has both, and they are different words: vin / bain, vous / bout. Try a long vvvv and feel the buzz in your lip.
b-v.sentence: Vous buvez un bon vin dans la ville, puis un bain au bout du couloir.

aspiration.title: p, t, k without a puff
aspiration.tip: At the start of a word, English p, t and k come with a puff of air. French p, t and k have none. Hold a piece of paper in front of your mouth: it mustn't move when you say papa, tout, café. The t is made with the tongue against your teeth, not behind them.
aspiration.sentence: Papa prend un café et une tarte au pain.

stress.title: No stressed syllable inside the word
stress.tip: French doesn't stress syllables inside a word. All syllables are about the same length, and only the last one of a group is a little longer and higher: cho-co-LAT, un cho-co-lat CHAUD. Tap an even beat and say the word on it. Don't push the first syllable, and don't make a vowel weak.
stress.sentence: Mon appartement est près de l'université.

double.title: One consonant, not two
double.tip: In French a double letter is only spelling: pomme, belle, année have one consonant of normal length. Don't hold it as in Italian. Say it quickly, in one go, and move on to the next vowel. A few exceptions mark a tense (il mourra, nous courrons), but for now: single.
double.sentence: Cette année, la belle pomme est bonne.

voiced-final.title: Keep the voice on at the end
voiced-final.tip: A French word can end in a voiced consonant (b, d, g, v, z, j): robe, rouge, bague, code. Keep your voice on until the end of the sound, and don't turn it into p, t, k, f, s or sch. bague and bac are two words, so are code and cote.
voiced-final.sentence: Elle a perdu sa bague dans le bac, puis note le code et la cote, sans honte.

p-b.title: p or b?
p-b.tip: p is a b without voice: close your lips, let the air out, and keep your throat quiet. b has voice from the start. French p has no puff of air. Put a finger on your throat: you feel a buzz for b and none for p.
p-b.sentence: Il n'y a pas de pain dans le bain, et la poule est en bas.

vowels.title: Pure vowels
vowels.tip: Say a vowel and keep your mouth in one position until the end. é is not “ay”, o is not “oh-oo”. Look in a mirror: your lips and jaw don't move while the vowel lasts. And keep the weak syllables full: the last a of café is a real a.
vowels.sentence: Elle a pris un café en été au bureau.

h.title: The silent h
h.tip: The letter h is never said in French: l'homme sounds like “lomme”. Begin right on the next vowel, and use no breath. h aspiré (le héros, les haricots) is silent too, but blocks the liaison and the elision.
h.sentence: L'homme habite à l'hôtel à huit heures.
